items.title: fix(core): governance pruning of requested-variant leaves can bypass subagent exclusions for retarget-added leaves (Codex P1 on #871)

comments.body:
## Intake review

**Related:** PR https://github.com/developing-today/opencode/pull/871 (Codex P1, head 07e72e8d48, packages/core/src/session/model-governance.ts); #869 (plugin-expansion pruning semantics this must not regress)

**Notes:** Filed 2026-10-29T13:56Z from a Codex P1 on PR #871, which is still OPEN — the bypass it describes is live in that PR's retarget path. Still live: no open or merged PR references #889. The issue body itself explains why it is not a one-line fix: #871 deliberately implements the opposite semantics for the catalog path.

**Risks:** A subagent exclusion that silently stops blocking a deployment is a governance/safety hole, not a cosmetic bug — hence priority/high. The fix must not break the deliberate #869 expansion pruning.

**Suggested approach:** Decide the reconciliation layer first (the issue lists the three candidate designs), then implement with the Codex scenario as the regression test.

🤖 **Agent note** · filed
- **Agent:** fleet monitor (repo-fleet-monitor)
- **Session / ID:** repo-fleet-monitor run 2026-10-29T14:30Z (09:30 CDT)
- **Found via:** monitor reconciliation
- **Task:** Duty 2 intake enrichment — acceptance criteria appended (original body preserved verbatim above it), labels normalized, `meta/enriched` applied. Still-live check this pass: no merged PR or fix commit explicitly resolving this issue was found; where a queue triage task owns verification, it is named in the notes.
- **Expectation:** see the effort label; done =

Verified against PR #871 head `d77f8128a4` (lane `openchamber-scheduled-lane`, task 3411): the bypass this issue describes is closed by the variant refresh in `203b8f7d1d`, so the issue is being closed as addressed by #871.

**The premise no longer holds.** The finding assumed "retargeting updates the route's settings but leaves its advertised variants unchanged". `retargetDefinition()` now returns `routeVariants(leaves)` computed over the post-transform leaves, and the model transform writes it back (`packages/core/src/config/plugin/model-routes.ts`, model transform: `draft.variants = variants`). When a transform adds a deployment that cannot produce the requested variant natively or through its remap, that variant leaves the route's advertised set.

**Consequence at resolution time.** `ModelResolver.resolveSelected()` rejects any requested variant the route does not advertise (`packages/core/src/model-resolver.ts` ~611: `if (requestedVariant && !selected.variants.some(...)) VariantUnavailableError`) before `resolveRoute()` picks a target. So the retarget-added deployment is never loaded with an undefined variant under that route variant, and an exclusion naming it has nothing to bypass: the run set is empty, not "the leaf runs bare". Governance pruning the same leaf is therefore consistent with the runtime — the judged set and the run set still agree.

**Regression coverage** (`packages/core/test/model-route-transform-models.test.ts`, "advertised variants after retargeting
